policy.note: design/09 §7.1/§7.4 (D36): the pinned judge identity — a judge record produced under any other identity is invalid. Three independent attempts; per-item verdict = 2-of-3 majority; any split item is marked flaky:true and is a RUBRIC defect to tighten. Overall verdict 'fail' iff any item fails; 'na' never fails a figure. CI never invokes the judge — T-JUDGE-RECORD (WP-17) gates on committed records at figures/<figure_id>.judge.json whose spec_hash/result_hash match the current figure and whose judge identity matches this file; missing or stale → exit 3. Editing this file invalidates every record → the §7.4 re-judge ceremony (one dedicated commit, every verdict flip enumerated).
re_judge_log: 2026-07-25 re-judge ceremony (design/09 §7.4). Trigger: D47/D48 changed what every figure DRAWS — the usable corridor (stage 3b), line chrome (stage 8b: the 10 m direction ladder, entry speeds, the outcome word, and fig 8.1's gated consequence ray) and the scale bar (stage 11) — so all six committed SVGs moved and all six prior records became records of images that no longer exist. Judged fresh, three passes each: the 2x colour raster, a second reading of the same raster for markers/labels/fabrication, and the GREYSCALE conversion, which is new and which the D47 outcome words exist to survive. Rasters retained under figures/png/. Verdict flips against the superseded records: NONE — every item that passed still passes, every `na` is still `na` (fig-08-02 and fig-08-06 declare no labels, so J3 stays na; only fig-08-01 has occluders, so J4 is pass there and na elsewhere; J6 is diagram-only and J9 is D45-gated, both na throughout). All six remain overall `pass`; no item is flaky. Two honest reservations are recorded in the evidence rather than hidden: fig-08-02's J5 passes on 'same turn point, did not turn' — the rate itself is a lean-vs-station fact that lives in the controls strip, so the top-down under-shows it without misleading; and fig-08-04's two lines are a single stroke in greyscale for the first 20 m, separating where the claim lives, at the tightening exit.

2026-07-29 re-judge, SCOPED TO ONE FIGURE (design/09 §7.4; NOT a §7.4 six-figure ceremony — this file's identity fields are untouched). Trigger: ROADMAP work order 1 restored one apex glyph on fig-08-05's `early` line, so its 2026-07-25 record became a record of an image that no longer exists and the suite went red on `svg_fnv1a` e80e05 vs 7e1dbd. WHICH RASTERIZER PRODUCED THE IMAGES, which the 2026-07-25 entry could take for granted and this one cannot: linelab/tools/rasterize-figures.mjs, built for this pass because design/09 §7 step 2's headless-browser rasterizer had never existed — puppeteer 25.4.0 driving its version-pinned Chrome for Testing, browser.version() = "Chrome/151.0.7922.47", 2x scale on a white background, sRGB forced, hinting and LCD text off; the two rasters and their sha256s are declared in figures/png/fig-08-05.raster.json and re-render byte-identical on repetition. Three passes, as in 2026-07-25: the 2x colour raster, a second reading of the same raster for markers/labels/fabrication, and the greyscale conversion. AND THE RASTER ITSELF IS A DIFFERENT IMAGE FROM THE ONE THE SUPERSEDED RECORD READ. The committed rasters carry their ink at 1x in the top-left quadrant of a 2x canvas — measured: fig-08-05's predecessor stops at (999, 1386) of 2000x2774, the new one reaches (1999, 2773) — so J8, "lines distinguishable and text readable at the 2x raster", was in fact graded at 1x throughout the 2026-07-25 ceremony. That is a reservation about the OLD evidence for all six figures, not a finding against the other five figures' SVGs, which are unchanged. VERDICT FLIPS against the superseded record, enumerated: J8 pass -> FAIL, and with it the overall verdict pass -> FAIL. Every other item is unmoved (J1/J2/J3/J5/J7 pass, J4/J6/J9 na). The J8 failure is a label collision, not a physics or colour problem, and it is on committed ink that predates this pass: the `30 m` direction-ladder label (stage 8b line chrome, SVG x=23.865 y=-12.881) sits on the same baseline as the callout "no geometry left for c2 - off the outside edge" (stage 10, text-anchor=end at x=24.735 y=-12.887) and is completely overprinted — zero glyphs of it survive in the raster, while 10/20/40/50/60 m are all crisply readable. Two of three passes graded it fail; the pass that graded it pass read the ladder at the overview scale. Recorded as SCOPE.md §4 S37 rather than repaired, because design/06 §3.1 stage 10 makes label boxes repel "each other and the road ink" and says nothing about stage-8b chrome, so the letter is SILENT on this collision and the repair is the design owner's call. TWO FLAKY ITEMS, which §7.4 makes rubric defects to tighten rather than figure defects: J5 (pass/pass/na — the greyscale pass returned `na` on mistake legibility with no ground, which the rubric permits it to do because it does not say J5 always applies to a figure drawing a mistake-role line) and J8 (pass/fail/fail — the rubric does not say at what magnification "readable" is decided, which is precisely the ambiguity the 1x-ink raster hid for three days). Both are recorded rather than smoothed. One further seam noted by the colour pass and left unrepaired: figures/fig-08-05.scene authors `view: mode=diagram` and the envelope's `meta.view.mode` carries that verbatim, while the bake renders `--mode true` and the manifest declares mode "true" — so a reader of `meta` alone is told the wrong mode, and J6 is `na` only because the manifest and the SVG's data-mode agree against `meta`.

rubric.name: colour-verdict
rubric.asserts: every line's rendered colour matches its manifest-declared verdict class under the D9 mapping

rubric.name: markers
rubric.asserts: hourglass turn-point / ring apex / dot exit present per the marks setting, each on its line, none floating

rubric.name: labels
rubric.asserts: every callout anchored at its declared anchor; none floating, clipped, or swallowed

rubric.name: sight grammar
rubric.asserts: when occluders are present: dashed rays from each line's eye to its limit point; occluded region shaded

rubric.name: mistake legibility
rubric.asserts: each mistake-role line visually reads as the error it teaches (the one genuinely judgmental item)

rubric.name: projection disclosure
rubric.asserts: diagram mode only: disclosure note present; the compressed figure still reads physically sensible
rubric.applies: diagram mode only — na on every v0.1 (true-mode) figure

rubric.name: no fabrication
rubric.asserts: nothing drawn that the manifest doesn't declare

rubric.name: legibility floor
rubric.asserts: lines distinguishable and text readable at the 2x raster

rubric.name: fan disclosure
rubric.asserts: a drawn continuation fan carries its disclosure; a cross-tick beyond FAN_DRAW_M renders clamped with the truncated hatch
rubric.applies: D45 render promotion only — absent from v0.1 judging

standing_sentence: a failing line's endpoint must sit at its termination — never wandering in the grass, never exiting the frame uncropped
